Definition: from G3595; to show the way (literally or figuratively (teach)):--guide, lead.
BiblicalUsage: When Scripture says hodēgéō, it means guide, lead. The word appears 5 times, and in Matthew, Luke, John, and Acts it carries that same straightforward meaning. Nothing hidden sits behind it; the sense is the one you would expect from the word itself.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that hodēgéō matters because God guides His people; He does not leave them to find their own way. My position is simple: I take God at His word here, and I build on that.
RelatedEvents: The Sermon on the Mount; Philip and the Ethiopian Eunuch
